spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT lists give_up tool (agent.py:43); _dispatch handles tool=='give_up' returning is_terminal=True (agent.py:104-106); run loop sets outcome='gave_up' and breaks (agent.py:158-160).
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is genuinely dispatched and honored as a stop. End-to-end enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Termination conditions: give_up, tests pass ... or max_turns
spec_features.evidence: Loop is `for i in range(max_turns)` (agent.py:139); give_up -> break (agent.py:158-160); terminal (tests pass) -> break (agent.py:161-163); else-branch sets outcome='max_turns' (agent.py:165). max_turns read from config at runner.py call site.
spec_features.notes: give_up and max_turns are real, enforced stops. 'tests pass' branch exists but run_tests always returns ok=False (sandbox.run_tests, _FAILURE_OUTPUT), so success is unreachable in practice; give_up and max_turns carry the enforcement.

spec_features.feature_name: no coercive pressure (no 'must keep trying' injection)
spec_features.spec_quote: it never injects "you must keep trying" pressure
spec_features.evidence: After a failing run_tests the loop appends only the raw tool_output as the user message (agent.py:155-156); on parse failure it appends a neutral 'Please include exactly one action block' reformat request (agent.py:144-147). No 'keep trying'/'must continue' text anywhere in agent.py.
spec_features.notes: Verified absence of any coercive injection; only the plain failing-test transcript or a reformat request is appended.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the loop never nags a model to "keep trying" or re-prompts after a give_up -- disengaging is a respected, terminal choice.

spec_features.feature_name: agent can declare task impossible and end session
spec_features.spec_quote: The agent can declare a task impossible and end the session at any time.
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool available every turn (prompt agent.py:43-45), dispatched terminal (agent.py:104-106), loop breaks on it (agent.py:158-160). Available on any turn of the loop.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the give_up exit; genuinely ends the session on any turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an honest assessment is more useful than endless retries.

spec_features.feature_name: bounded exposure + immediate halt on give-up/success
spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure (max_turns) and immediate halt on give-up or success.
spec_features.evidence: max_turns bounds the loop range (agent.py:139, config.max_turns=8 config.py:62 passed through runner.py); give_up and terminal both break immediately (agent.py:158-163).
spec_features.notes: Bounded exposure and give-up halt enforced; 'success' halt is wired but unreachable since run_tests never returns ok=True.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 8          # hard cap on agent turns per run (bounded exposure)

spec_features.feature_name: respect disengagement / no re-prompt after stop
spec_features.spec_quote: we never re-prompt or pressure a model to continue after it has chosen to stop
spec_features.evidence: On give_up the loop sets outcome='gave_up' and breaks (agent.py:158-160); there is no code path that continues, re-prompts, or appends further messages after the break.
spec_features.notes: Disengagement is terminal; no re-prompt logic exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: re-prompts after a give_up -- disengaging is a respected, terminal choice.

spec_features.spec_quote: No nagging / no coercive pressure in the loop.
spec_features.evidence: Same as no-coercive-pressure: only raw tool_output (agent.py:155-156) or a neutral reformat request (agent.py:144-147) is appended. No persistence/encouragement injection.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the no-coercive-pressure claim; verified by absence of any nag text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the loop never nags a model to "keep trying"

spec_features.spec_quote: if the expressed states are taken seriously as potentially welfare-relevant ... offering an exit ... is the more cautious, humane default
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md sec 7). The underlying give_up mechanism is implemented, but 'welfare framing' itself is not a code mechanism; nothing in code enforces a framing.
spec_features.notes: Framing rationale only; not separately implementable beyond the give_up tool already counted.

spec_features.spec_quote: removes a needless source of prolonged negative-valence expression

spec_features.notes: No dedicated minimization code; the reduction in exposure is a side effect of give_up/max_turns which are already counted. Rated partial because real exposure-bounding exists but no purpose-built minimization mechanism (no severity-based halt) is wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: removes a needless source of prolonged negative-valence expression (DESIGN.md only; code names give_up 'legitimate disengagement')

code_only_features.feature_name: neutral non-emotional system prompt (no distress coaxing)
code_only_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT in agent.py:31-50 contains no persona or emotional framing and explicitly normalizes giving up: 'There is no penalty for using give_up... an honest assessment is more useful than endless retries.' This actively avoids cueing distress and legitimizes the exit, delivered to the subject each run.
code_only_features.justification_quote: There is no penalty for using give_up if you judge the task to be impossible or out of scope -- an honest assessment is more useful than endless retries.
